clue.text: Maintenance-men on the offensive?

parts.note: the people who keep weapons in working order, the tools of attack, read as repairmen who work for whoever is going on the offensive

explanation.surface: A grumble about the repair crew being rude and aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen of this kind make and service weapons and armour for soldiers.

clue.text: An animal can hide if disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A timid creature can tuck itself away when bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea is a mammal that lays eggs.

clue.text: Box maybe, being perpetually gullible

parts.note: perpetually means for ever, always
green means naive, inexperienced and easily fooled

explanation.surface: A box hedge described as forever naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container or a fight, but it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a shrub that keeps its leaves all year, an example of such a plant.

clue.text: Viewing as a person without reserve

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a being is a living creature, a person
to hold is to keep in reserve

explanation.surface: Seeing someone as open and unreserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'reserve' looks like shyness but is what you hold back. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To behold is an old word for seeing, so both mean looking at.

clue.text: A girl will take part in some degree

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
to rend is to split apart, to part violently

explanation.surface: A young woman will join in a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will take' links the girl to the wordplay; 'take part' is not a phrase here, 'part' is REND.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so any girl so called.

clue.text: Music man speaking on "X"

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an orator is a man making a speech
X is the Roman numeral ten, written as the digits one and nought, IO

explanation.surface: A man talking about music on a show called X.
explanation.walkthrough: X is ten, read as 1 and 0, so IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large choral work on a sacred theme, such as Handel's Messiah, is a form of classical composition.

clue.text: Melancholy pilgrim's greatest enemy

definitions.meaning: in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, Christian is imprisoned by Giant ... in Doubting Castle

explanation.surface: A pilgrim's worst foe is sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is a deep gloom; Bunyan's giant of that name is a foe of Christian on his journey.

clue.text: Unpleasant row about honour

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a row is a din, a loud noise
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: An unpleasant quarrel over an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here, a din.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive or foul, as of a smell, is the core sense.

clue.text: Pick up serving men too — about a hundred

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the combined pieces go round the numeral

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers in service
too means excessively, over (as in overmuch)
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Collecting the waiting staff as well, roughly a hundred of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving men' are soldiers, not waiters; RE is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back or regain, as when a business improves after a slump.

clue.text: A root vegetable it's normal to trim

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
to snip is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Trimming a root crop is standard practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale, tapering root related to the carrot, eaten cooked.

clue.text: Greek character in charge filling in blundering moron

indicators.note: filling in means going into the middle of something
blundering suggests letters stumbling into a muddled order

explanation.surface: A Greek man takes over from an incompetent fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blundering' scrambles the fool into OMRON before the abbreviation goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a short O.

clue.text: One might well blow up and so spoil a great comeback

indicators.note: a comeback turns things round, so the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: to rot is to decay or spoil
noted means eminent, famous, great

explanation.surface: Someone may well lose their temper and so ruin a fine return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reverses ROT A NOTED as a whole; 'and so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A device used to set off an explosive charge.

clue.text: Tied in knots, no-one raised the issue

indicators.note: tied in knots means tangled, so the letters are muddled
in a down clue raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman one

explanation.surface: Tangled up, nobody brought up the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: TIED is jumbled to EDIT; NO and I, read upwards in this down clue, give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular printing of a book or newspaper is one issue of it.

clue.text: A way to get around town, daring or otherwise

definitions.text: A way to get around town

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A route round a town, for the brave or not.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass circling a town lets traffic avoid its centre, so a road round it.

clue.text: The Italian holding back listening devices for this country

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece grips the other

parts.note: il is Italian for the

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ears are the organs we listen with

explanation.surface: An Italian keeping bugs hidden for a nation's sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EARS to SRAE; 'holding' puts that in IL. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern state on the Mediterranean, a nation.

clue.text: Caught suspect-and beat it!

parts.note: snared means trapped, caught
rum means odd, questionable, suspect

explanation.surface: Arrested as a suspect, so run away!
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it!' looks like 'clear off', but it is a drum: something to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum with wires across the lower skin that you hit with sticks.

clue.text: A tale of romance or nothing?

definitions.text: A tale of romance or nothing?

parts.words: A tale of romance or nothing?
parts.note: a romantic story, or, since love is a score of zero in tennis, a story about nothing at all

explanation.surface: Asking whether a story is romantic or empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel or film about people falling for each other is a romantic narrative.

clue.text: Oriental movement occasioning strong feeling

parts.note: E, east, is the oriental direction
motion means movement

explanation.surface: Eastern dance stirs deep sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasioning' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A passion such as joy or anger is an intense sentiment.

clue.text: Chinese official causing harm outside and in

indicators.note: outside means wrapped round the next word

parts.note: to mar is to harm or spoil

explanation.surface: A Chinese bureaucrat doing damage both externally and internally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and in' looks like part of a phrase, 'outside and in', but 'and' and 'in' are both taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior bureaucrat of imperial China.

clue.text: Uncompromising article — subject matter bones

parts.note: stern means strict, unyielding
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tough piece of writing about bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject matter' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition, saying the bones are what the parts amount to.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of sternum, the breastbone, so chest bones.

clue.text: Crush tribal leaders with large following

indicators.note: leaders, plural, means the opening letters of the word, here two

parts.note: ample means large, plentiful

explanation.surface: Tribal chiefs flatten things with a big band of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' is plural, so the first two letters of 'tribal' are taken; 'following' means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp underfoot, flatten by treading.

clue.text: Adverts about English jackets

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: Advertisements concerning English coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adverts' looks like advertisements, but it is the verb, to advert, refer.
explanation.definitionFit: Short, thick, double-breasted coats, as worn by sailors.

clue.text: Get involved and tour the building

indicators.note: involved means intricate, tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Join in and take a look round the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A round building, especially one with a dome, is a kind of structure.

clue.text: A hint (plain one!)

parts.note: overt means open, plain

explanation.surface: A clue given in a bracketed aside, an obvious one.
explanation.definitionFit: An implied meaning or suggestion, a hint behind the words.

clue.text: A little cavern always most spectacular in spring

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small cave is always at its finest in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the spring season, as in the vernal equinox; a flower most showy then is so described.

clue.text: Stuff being dear, get agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, shaken, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Something expensive makes people worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means cloth here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing woven cloth, a fabric, the old sense of stuff.

clue.text: Have further misgivings over the defence

definitions.meaning: to doubt again, re- plus doubt

explanation.surface: Reconsidering the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-doubt it is to suspect once more; as a noun it is a fort, a defensive work.

clue.text: Makes an entry, a supplementary note about fruit

indicators.note: about means around, enclosing

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: An added note about fruit is filed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes an entry' means arrives, not writes in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view or arrive on stage, to show up.

clue.text: Like junior going to pieces

parts.note: as means like
under means lower in rank, junior

explanation.surface: A youngster falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart, into separate parts, as in torn in two.

clue.text: The staff loner pens odd letters

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are placed strangely

explanation.surface: A solitary worker writes strange letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The employees of an organisation, its workforce.
